With this, we are able to show that efficient quantum algorithms exist for a much wider class of nonlinear systems than previously known, and prove the BQP-completeness of nonlinear oscillator problems of exponential size. In our analysis, we also obtain several results related to the Poincaré-Dulac theorem and diagonalization of the Carleman matrix, which could be of independent interest.

.
tldr: The paper develops quantum algorithms for simulating broad classes of nonlinear dynamics using Carleman embedding, extending prior results beyond purely dissipative systems and proving BQP-completeness for nonlinear oscillator problems.
motivation: Nonlinear dynamics in fluids and plasmas are hard to simulate classically, and earlier quantum algorithms based on Carleman embedding were limited to dissipative systems with negative log-norm.
method: The authors correct prior technical analysis and extend convergence criteria using quadratic Lyapunov functions, conserved polynomial quantities, and non-resonant system classes, with additional results on the Poincaré-Dulac theorem and diagonalization of the Carleman matrix.
result: They establish efficient quantum algorithms for a much wider class of stable nonlinear systems and prove BQP-completeness for exponentially large nonlinear oscillator problems.
conclusion: This significantly broadens the scope of nonlinear dynamical systems amenable to efficient quantum simulation, though it is primarily a quantum-algorithms/complexity contribution rather than a core quantum-information result.

title: Van Der Waals Superconducting Electronics: Materials, Devices And Circuit Integration
authors: A Di Bernardo And E Scheer
abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) superconductors (SCs)—atomically thin crystalline materials that can be stacked into more complex heterostructures—have opened a promising avenue for superconducting electronics thanks to their properties that are otherwise difficult to obtain in other superconducting materials. These properties include strong resilience to high in-plane magnetic fields, electrostatic tuneability, and non-reciprocal transport rooted in inversion-symmetry breaking and strong spin–orbit coupling. In addition to highlighting the importance of these properties for superconducting electronics, this review gives an overview of the physical mechanisms that govern and influence superconductivity in vdW materials including Ising pairing, band inversion, and proximity effects at SC/ferromagnet interfaces that do not have an equivalent in thin-film systems. This overview then sets the basis to survey the wide range of functionalities enabled by superconducting vdW devices including gate-controlled devices, superconducting diodes, and circuit elements for readout and control of quantum bits. The review concludes with a forward look at wafer-scale growth and deterministic assembly of vdW devices, highlighting concrete pathways that can enable the transition from vdW device prototypes to deployable components for cryogenic electronics and quantum technologies.
tldr: This review surveys van der Waals superconductors and their device/circuit applications for superconducting electronics and cryogenic quantum technologies.
motivation: Van der Waals superconductors offer properties difficult to achieve in conventional thin-film superconductors, such as high in-plane magnetic-field resilience, electrostatic tunability, and non-reciprocal transport, motivating their use in superconducting electronics.
method: The authors review physical mechanisms governing superconductivity in vdW materials, including Ising pairing, band inversion, and superconductor/ferromagnet proximity effects, and survey device functionalities such as gate-controlled devices, superconducting diodes, and qubit readout/control circuit elements.
result: The review identifies promising vdW material properties and device demonstrations, while emphasizing challenges in wafer-scale growth and deterministic assembly needed for deployable cryogenic electronics.
conclusion: Van der Waals superconducting electronics could enable new cryogenic and quantum-technology components, but the field remains at a materials-and-device-prototype stage with integration challenges ahead.

title: Floquet-ADAPT-VQE: A Quantum Algorithm To Simulate Non-Equilibrium Physics In Periodically Driven Systems
authors: Abhishek Kumar, Karunya Shirali, Nicholas J. Mayhall, Sophia E. Economou, And Edwin Barnes
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2247 (2026).

Periodically driven quantum systems exhibit many fascinating phenomena absent in equilibrium systems, but their simulation is more challenging than that of static systems. Consequently, quantum simulation of these systems offers greater opportunity for achieving quantum advantage. To build the foundation for simulating time-periodic Hamiltonians, we utilize the Floquet-Hilbert space formalism to transform the Hamiltonian into a time-independent form and provide its Pauli decomposition. Within this formalism, we develop a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm, Floquet-ADAPT-VQE, that produces three key quantities that govern periodically driven quantum dynamics: the quasienergy, the associated Floquet eigenstates, and expectation values of observables with respect to these eigenstates. The latter is achieved by applying a fixed-depth quantum circuit to an initial Floquet eigenstate—an efficient construction made possible by the Floquet-Hilbert space formalism. We also identify a suitable auxiliary initial state whose squared Floquet energy is independent of the number of auxiliary qubits as well as the driving frequency, which leads to better convergence with fewer ADAPT iterations. We demonstrate our algorithm by performing numerical simulations on a periodically driven XYZ model with a magnetic field. We also explore potential applications of our algorithm for studying various non-equilibrium phenomena in periodically driven systems.

.
tldr: The authors introduce Floquet-ADAPT-VQE, a hybrid quantum-classical variational algorithm for computing quasienergies, Floquet eigenstates, and observables of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Simulating time-periodic Hamiltonians is more challenging than static systems, and periodically driven systems offer a promising route to quantum advantage, motivating a dedicated simulation algorithm.
method: They use the Floquet-Hilbert space formalism to map the driven Hamiltonian to a time-independent Pauli form and combine it with ADAPT-VQE, including an auxiliary initial state designed to improve convergence.
result: Numerical simulations on a periodically driven XYZ model with a magnetic field demonstrate the algorithm's ability to produce quasienergies, Floquet eigenstates, and observable expectation values.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for quantum simulation of non-equilibrium Floquet physics, but it is primarily an algorithmic/quantum-simulation contribution rather than a direct information-thermodynamics result.

title: A Symmetry-Enabled Direct Quantum Protocol For Many-Body Green’s Functions
authors: Changhao Yi And Cunlu Zhou
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2245 (2026).

We present a symmetry-enabled direct quantum protocol for computing many-body Green's functions, a central tool for studying strongly correlated quantum systems. Our protocol relies only on native time evolution and straightforward measurements available on current hardware platforms. By exploiting parity symmetry—satisfied by a broad class of Hamiltonians in condensed matter physics and quantum chemistry, including the Fermi–Hubbard and Heisenberg models—we introduce a tailored quench spectroscopy scheme that recovers both the real and imaginary parts of two-point time correlators, from which Green's functions can be reconstructed via efficient classical signal processing. We further develop a tailored symmetric quantum Gibbs sampler that prepares parity-resolved (symmetric and antisymmetric) thermal states, enabling finite-temperature extensions within the same framework. Finally, we show that the same symmetry-based measurement primitive extends naturally to out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). Our results provide a practical route to estimating symmetry-resolved dynamical correlators on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

.
tldr: The paper proposes a symmetry-enabled quantum protocol that uses native time evolution and simple measurements to reconstruct many-body Green's functions, including finite-temperature and out-of-time-ordered correlator extensions.
motivation: Many-body Green's functions are central to strongly correlated physics and chemistry but are hard to extract on near-term quantum hardware, which typically lacks the resources for full signal-processing-heavy approaches.
method: Exploiting parity symmetry (valid for Hubbard, Heisenberg, and similar models), the authors design a tailored quench-spectroscopy scheme measuring two-point time correlators, plus a symmetry-resolved quantum Gibbs sampler for thermal states, with classical post-processing to reconstruct real and imaginary parts.
result: The protocol recovers both real and imaginary components of two-point correlators from simple measurement primitives, extends to finite temperature via parity-resolved thermal state preparation, and adapts naturally to OTOCs.
conclusion: The work offers a practical, hardware-friendly route to symmetry-resolved dynamical correlators on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum devices.

title: Measuring Spin-charge Separation By An Off-diagonal Dissipative Response
authors: Shi Chen And Yu Chen Liang Tong
abstract: Spin-charge separation in the 1D Hubbard model is a paradigmatic example of quantum fractionalization described by decoupled charge and spin sectors of a Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid. Despite the success in measuring velocity differences, it remains challenging to probe emergent excitations’ anomalous dimensions experimentally. We propose an off-diagonal dissipative response protocol, leveraging dissipative response theory, to directly detect spin-charge separation. By selectively dissipating spin- particles and measuring the spin- response, we uncover a universal temporal crossover: the response grows as at short times and crosses over to linear-in- growth at long times. Specifically, the intersection time between the short-time and long-time linear growth exhibits a linear dependence on , whose slope is proportional to with a prefactor that depends on the filling , with negligible residual dependence on over a broad parameter range. This prefactor cancels when comparing slopes at a fixed , allowing the relative variation of with interaction strength to be extracted directly without any absolute calibration. Concurrently, the coefficient of the short-time law encodes the sum of anomalous dimensions through its spatial power-law decay. This response signal vanishes in the noninteracting limit, where spin and charge are not separated. Our predictions, verified numerically via time-dependent density-matrix renormalization group with microscopic parameters linked to Luttinger parameters by Bethe-ansatz, establish off-diagonal dissipative response as a self-contained probe of quantum fractionalization in synthetic quantum matter.
tldr: The authors propose an off-diagonal dissipative response protocol to detect spin-charge separation in the 1D Hubbard model, verified with time-dependent DMRG.
motivation: Spin-charge separation in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids is well established in terms of velocity differences, but probing the anomalous dimensions of emergent excitations remains experimentally challenging.
method: A dissipative response theory scheme that selectively dissipates spin-1/2 particles and measures the resulting spin response is analyzed numerically using time-dependent density-matrix renormalization group, with microscopic parameters matched to Luttinger parameters via Bethe ansatz.
result: The response shows a universal short-time power-law growth crossing over to linear-in-time growth, with a crossover time scaling proportional to a parameter whose slope encodes interaction-dependent Luttinger exponents; the spatial decay of the short-time law yields the sum of anomalous dimensions, and the signal vanishes in the noninteracting limit.
conclusion: Off-diagonal dissipative response is established as a self-contained, calibration-free probe of quantum fractionalization in synthetic quantum matter.

title: Topological Tricritical Ising Universality Class In One Dimension
authors: Hai-Qing Lin And Xue-Jia Yu Sheng Yang
abstract: Quantum critical points can host symmetry-protected topological (SPT) edge modes even when the bulk is gapless, giving rise to symmetry-enriched universality classes beyond the conventional Landau–Ginzburg–Wilson paradigm. Here we show that the tricritical Ising (TCI) critical point—described by a paradigmatic conformal field theory (CFT) with emergent supersymmetry—admits a topologically nontrivial, symmetry-enriched realization, which we term the topological TCI. We construct this critical point in the cluster O’Brien–Fendley (OF) spin chain by applying an SPT entangler to the original OF model. The two realizations therefore share the same bulk TCI CFT. Under open boundary conditions, however, the original model exhibits the free conformal boundary condition, whereas the cluster model exhibits a spontaneously fixed boundary condition: an infinitesimal boundary field can select one of the fixed boundary states, yielding spontaneous boundary magnetization. We further show that symmetry enrichment and boundary renormalization-group flow provide two routes to the spontaneously fixed boundary condition. Whereas the free and spontaneously fixed boundary conditions of the original model can be interconverted by tuning a symmetry-preserving boundary term, no such conversion occurs for the cluster model along the boundary deformations studied here, even in the strong-deformation limit. Although they share the same conventional boundary CFT (BCFT) data, including the boundary operator content and boundary -function, the two realizations of the spontaneously fixed boundary condition are distinguished by different time-reversal charges of the disorder field, which impose different symmetry constraints on the allowed boundary conditions under symmetry-preserving boundary deformations. For the tested symmetry-preserving boundary perturbations that lift the exact twofold degeneracy, the finite-size energy splitting is numerically consistent with exponential decay over accessible system sizes, in stark contrast to the algebraic splitting at the symmetry-enriched Ising critical point of the cluster Ising spin chain. We also find that the topological TCI realization persists along a critical line in a two-parameter phase diagram. These results establish a symmetry-enriched TCI universality class and uncover boundary distinctions invisible to conventional BCFT data.
tldr: The authors construct a symmetry-enriched 'topological' tricritical Ising critical point in a cluster O'Brien–Fendley spin chain and show that, despite sharing bulk CFT and conventional boundary CFT data with the original model, it exhibits a spontaneously fixed boundary condition distinguished by time-reversal charges.
motivation: Quantum critical points can host symmetry-protected topological edge modes even with a gapless bulk, raising the question of whether paradigmatic CFTs such as the supersymmetric tricritical Ising point admit topologically nontrivial, symmetry-enriched realizations with distinct boundary physics.
method: An SPT entangler is applied to the original O'Brien–Fendley chain to build the cluster model sharing the same bulk TCI CFT; boundary conditions, boundary RG flows, and finite-size energy splittings under symmetry-preserving boundary perturbations are analyzed analytically and numerically, including a two-parameter phase diagram.
result: The cluster realization shows a spontaneously fixed boundary condition (spontaneous boundary magnetization) with exponential finite-size splitting, in contrast to the algebraic splitting of the symmetry-enriched Ising point, and cannot be converted to the free boundary condition by the studied deformations; the topological TCI persists along a critical line.
conclusion: A symmetry-enriched TCI universality class is established, revealing boundary distinctions invisible to conventional boundary CFT data such as boundary operator content and g-function.

title: Towards Local And Compositional Measurements In Quantum Field Theory
authors: Robert Oeckl And Adamantia Zampeli
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2232 (2026).

A universal framework for the joint measurement of multiple localized observables in quantum field theory satisfying spacetime locality and compositionality is still lacking. We present an approach to the problem that is based on the one hand on the positive formalism, an axiomatic framework, where it is clear from the outset that we satisfy locality and compositionality, while also having a consistent probabilistic interpretation. On the other hand, the approach is based on standard tools from quantum field theory, in particular the path integral and the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. After an overview of the conceptual foundations we introduce the modulus-square construction as a formalization of the measurement process for the expectation value of an important class of observables including quadratic observables. We show that this construction has many of the desired properties, including positivity, locality, single measurement recovery and compositionality. We introduce a renormalization scheme for the measurement of quadratic observables that also satisfies compositionality, in contrast to previous renormalization schemes. We discuss relativistic causality, confirming that measurements in our scheme are indeed localized in the spacetime regions where the underlying observables have support.

.
tldr: The paper proposes a formal framework for local and compositional joint measurements in quantum field theory using the positive formalism and Schwinger-Keldysh techniques.
motivation: A universal framework for measuring multiple localized observables in QFT while preserving spacetime locality, compositionality, and a consistent probabilistic interpretation is still missing.
method: The authors combine the positive formalism with path-integral and Schwinger-Keldysh tools, introducing a modulus-square construction for measurement expectation values and a compositional renormalization scheme for quadratic observables.
result: The construction satisfies positivity, locality, single-measurement recovery, and compositionality, and the proposed renormalization scheme preserves compositionality unlike previous schemes.
conclusion: The framework provides a consistent localized measurement scheme in QFT and clarifies relativistic causality for such measurements, though it is foundational rather than aligned with the specified quantum information research directions.

title: The Resource Theory Of Causal Influence And Knowledge Of Causal Influence
authors: Marina Maciel Ansanelli, Beata Zjawin, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, John H Selby, Ciarán M Gilligan-Lee, Ana Belén Sainz And Robert W Spekkens
abstract: Understanding and quantifying causal relationships between variables is essential for reasoning about the physical world. A challenge to this is the fact that different functional causal models can induce the same conditional probability distribution over observed variables while encoding different amounts of causal influence. Motivated by this observation, we study the underlying functional mechanisms, including uncertainty over them, as meaningful objects in their own right and develop a resource-theoretic framework for quantifying causal influence and knowledge of causal influence. We focus on the simplest nontrivial setting—two variables that are causally ordered, meaning that the first has the potential to influence the second, without hidden confounding. First, we introduce the resource theory that directly quantifies causal influence of a functional dependence in this setting and show that the problem of deciding convertibility of resources and identifying a complete set of monotones has a relatively straightforward solution. Following this, we introduce the resource theory that arises naturally when one has uncertainty about the functional dependence. We describe a linear program for deciding the question of whether one resource (i.e. state of knowledge about the functional dependence) can be converted to another. Then, we focus on the case where the variables are binary. In this case, we identify a triple of monotones that are complete in the sense that they capture the partial order over the set of all resources, and we provide an interpretation of each.
tldr: The paper develops a resource-theoretic framework for quantifying causal influence and knowledge of causal influence in functional causal models with two causally ordered variables.
motivation: Different functional causal models can induce the same observed conditional probabilities while encoding different amounts of causal influence, so the underlying functional mechanisms and uncertainty over them are studied as meaningful objects.
method: The authors introduce resource theories for causal influence and for knowledge of causal influence, analyze convertibility and monotones, provide a linear program for resource conversion under uncertainty, and specialize to binary variables.
result: They give a straightforward solution to convertibility and complete monotones for direct causal influence, a linear-program criterion for convertibility under uncertainty, and a complete triple of monotones for binary variables with interpretations.
conclusion: The work provides a resource-theoretic account of causal influence and epistemic uncertainty about causal mechanisms, but it is not directly framed as a quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems contribution.

title: Non-Hermitian Rayleigh–Schrödinger-like Perturbation Theory At Exceptional Point
authors: Wei-Ming Chen And Chia-Yi Ju
abstract: We develop a Rayleigh–Schrödinger-like perturbation theory for non-Hermitian quantum systems at an exceptional point (EP) of order . Working in the Jordan basis of the unperturbed Hamiltonian and employing a Puiseux expansion of the perturbed eigenvalues and eigenstates, we derive explicit recursion relations for the expansion coefficients. The corrections to the unperturbed eigenvalue in the Puiseux expansion govern the splitting near the EP; the first two are obtained iteratively in two equivalent forms. One is given in terms of the perturbation Hamiltonian in the Jordan basis, and the other in terms of the generator that drives the eigenvalue evolution with respect to the perturbation. The latter constitutes the exceptional-point counterpart of a geometric perturbation method recently developed for the non-exceptional-point regime. Both representations are verified explicitly for the and cases. We then apply the theory to an order-3 EP realized in a dissipative three-level trapped-ion system.
tldr: The paper develops a non-Hermitian Rayleigh–Schrödinger-like perturbation theory at exceptional points and applies it to a dissipative three-level trapped-ion system.
motivation: Exceptional points in non-Hermitian quantum systems require specialized perturbative methods because standard Hermitian perturbation theory fails when eigenvalues and eigenstates coalesce.
method: The authors work in the Jordan basis of the unperturbed Hamiltonian and use a Puiseux expansion to derive recursive relations for eigenvalue and eigenstate corrections, with two equivalent representations verified in low-order cases.
result: Explicit corrections governing eigenvalue splitting near an exceptional point are obtained and validated, including an application to an order-3 exceptional point in a dissipative trapped-ion system.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic perturbation framework for non-Hermitian systems at exceptional points, extending geometric perturbation methods to the exceptional-point regime.

title: Sampled-Based Guided Quantum Walk: Non-variational Quantum Algorithm For Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Ugo Nzongani, Dylan Laplace Mermoud, Giuseppe Di Molfetta, And Andrea Simonetto
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2234 (2026).

We introduce SamBa-GQW, a novel quantum algorithm for solving binary combinatorial optimization problems of arbitrary degree with no use of any classical optimizer. The algorithm is based on a continuous-time quantum walk on the solution space represented as a graph. The walker explores the solution space to find its way to vertices that minimize the cost function of the optimization problem. The key novelty of our algorithm is an offline classical sampling protocol that gives information about the spectrum of the problem Hamiltonian. Then, the extracted information is used to guide the walker to high quality solutions via a quantum walk with a time-dependent hopping rate. We investigate the performance of SamBa-GQW on several quadratic problems, namely MaxCut, maximum independent set, portfolio optimization, and higher-order polynomial problems such as LABS, MAX-[MATH]-SAT and a quartic reformulation of the travelling salesperson problem. We empirically demonstrate that SamBa-GQW finds high quality approximate solutions on problems up to a size of [MATH] qubits by only sampling poly([MATH]) states among [MATH] possible decisions. Furthermore, SamBa-GQW compares in par with classically optimized variational approaches, such as the variational guided quantum walk and QAOA (the latter when run on deep circuits). This places Samba-GQW as a promising heuristic to tackle combinatorial problems beyond the NISQ regime.

.
tldr: SamBa-GQW is a non-variational quantum algorithm that uses a continuous-time quantum walk with a time-dependent hopping rate, guided by an offline classical sampling of the problem Hamiltonian's spectrum, to approximately solve binary combinatorial optimization problems.
motivation: Existing quantum heuristics for combinatorial optimization, such as QAOA and variational guided quantum walks, rely on costly classical outer-loop optimization that becomes impractical beyond the NISQ regime; the authors seek an optimizer-free alternative.
method: The solution space is represented as a graph on which a continuous-time quantum walk evolves, with a hopping rate modulated in time by information extracted from an offline classical sampling protocol that probes the spectrum of the problem Hamiltonian, so the walker is steered toward low-cost vertices.
result: Applied to MaxCut, maximum independent set, portfolio optimization, LABS, MAX-k-SAT and a quartic TSP reformulation, the algorithm finds high-quality approximate solutions for instances up to dozens of qubits while sampling only polynomially many states, comparing favorably with classically optimized variational approaches and deep-circuit QAOA.
conclusion: Sampled-based guided quantum walks offer a promising variational-free heuristic for combinatorial optimization that could remain viable beyond the NISQ regime.

title: The Chiral Random Walk: A Quantum-inspired Framework For Odd Diffusion
authors: Jan Wójcik And Erik Kalz
abstract: Chirality in active and passive fluids gives rise to odd transport properties, most notably the emergence of robust edge currents that defy standard dissipative dynamics. While these phenomena are well-described by continuum hydrodynamics, the topological analogy with quantum systems, widely invoked to explain their robustness, has lacked a concrete discrete realization. Here, we present a lattice model for an isotropic chiral random walk that bridges the gap between classical stochastic diffusion and unitary quantum evolution. By equipping the walker with an internal degree of freedom and a tunable chirality parameter, , we interpolate between a standard diffusive random walk and a deterministic, topologically non-trivial quantum walk. We show that signatures of the topologically protected edge states characteristic of the unitary limit ( ) persist into the dissipative regime ( ) This correspondence allows us to theoretically ground the robustness of edge flows in classical chiral systems using the bulk-boundary correspondence of Floquet topological insulators. Our results provide a discrete, effective description for odd diffusion, offering a powerful toolkit to predict transport in confined geometries and disordered chiral media.
tldr: The paper introduces a lattice model of a chiral random walk that interpolates between classical diffusion and a topologically nontrivial quantum walk, using Floquet topological insulator bulk-boundary correspondence to explain robust edge currents in chiral fluids.
motivation: Chirality in active and passive fluids produces odd transport and robust edge currents, but a concrete discrete model linking these classical phenomena to quantum topological robustness has been missing.
method: The authors equip a random walker on a lattice with an internal degree of freedom and a tunable chirality parameter, constructing an isotropic chiral random walk that connects stochastic diffusion to unitary quantum walks and analyzing edge states via Floquet topological insulator theory.
result: They show that signatures of topologically protected edge states from the unitary quantum-walk limit persist into the dissipative regime, providing a discrete effective description of odd diffusion and edge-flow robustness.
conclusion: The chiral random walk offers a quantum-inspired toolkit for predicting transport in confined geometries and disordered chiral media, grounding classical odd diffusion in topological bulk-boundary correspondence.

title: Grey-body Factors Of Black Holes *
authors: Roman A Konoplya And Alexander Zhidenko
abstract: Grey-body factors describe the frequency-dependent transmission of fields through the effective potential generated by a black hole or another compact object. They convert the idealized thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation into the spectrum measured by an observer, determine absorption and scattering cross sections, and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes. In this review, we present a unified account of grey-body factors in black-hole physics and related systems. We formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, and discuss the connections between transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, and ringdown. We also review methods for their computation and survey recent developments, including the correspondence between grey-body factors and quasinormal modes, their stability under deformations of the effective potential, wormhole transmission and superradiance, and their behaviour in modified theories of gravity. Finally, we discuss the appearance of grey-body factors in gauge/gravity duality, where absorption probabilities in the bulk are related to correlation functions and transport coefficients in the boundary theory.
tldr: This review provides a unified treatment of grey-body factors for black holes and related compact objects, covering scattering, absorption, Hawking radiation, and connections to quasinormal modes and gauge/gravity duality.
motivation: Grey-body factors convert idealized Hawking spectra into observable spectra and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes, motivating a comprehensive review across spacetimes and modified gravity.
method: The authors formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, review computational methods for transmission coefficients and absorption cross sections, and survey recent developments.
result: The review connects grey-body factors to quasinormal modes, studies their stability under potential deformations, and discusses wormhole transmission, superradiance, modified gravity, and holographic applications.
conclusion: Grey-body factors are central to black-hole phenomenology and provide useful links between scattering, ringdown, and boundary correlation functions, but the work is outside the specified quantum-information-focused research directions.

title: Collective Excitations In Quantum Gravity Condensates
authors: Adrià Delhom And Daniele Oriti Andrea Calcinari
abstract: A central open problem in quantum gravity is to understand how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom in a background-independent setting. A many-body perspective suggests that spacetime emerges as a hydrodynamic phase of many atoms of quantum geometry. This idea underlies several approaches to quantum gravity, and it has been explicitly realised in the group field theory formalism. However, quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field regime remain largely unexplored. We fill this gap by importing Bogolyubov theory to quantum gravity condensates, showing that leading beyond-mean-field effects manifest as collective excitations, in direct analogy with phonons in laboratory Bose–Einstein condensates. We implement the construction in a tractable group field theory model, where condensates of quantum-geometric atoms reproduce nonsingular expanding cosmologies, and derive the leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics. These results identify a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establish a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence.

motivation: A central open problem in quantum gravity is how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom, and beyond-mean-field quantum fluctuations in quantum gravity condensates remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors import Bogoliubov theory from many-body physics into a tractable group field theory model of quantum gravity condensates and derive leading beyond-mean-field corrections.
result: They show that leading beyond-mean-field effects appear as collective excitations analogous to phonons in Bose-Einstein condensates and obtain corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics.
conclusion: The work identifies a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establishes a bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and spacetime emergence.

title: Two Phase Transitions In Modular Multiplex Networks
authors: Yael Kfir-Cohen, Dana Ben Porath, Bnaya Gross, Sergey Buldyrev And Shlomo Havlin
abstract: Modular networks, such as critical infrastructures, are often built from distinct, densely connected modules (e.g. cities) that are sparsely interconnected. When such networks are gradually and randomly disrupted under a percolation process, they undergo two critical phase transitions. The first transition occurs when modules become isolated from one another, while the second corresponds to the collapse of the entire network, including the internal connectivity of the modules. Here, we study these phase transitions in modular multiplex networks and compare them with those observed in single-layer modular networks. We focus on models in which the modules are arranged and connected either as a short-range two-dimensional square lattice or as a long-range random regular (RR) network. We show here that these systems exhibit diverse transition behaviors, with some transitions occurring continuously and others abruptly; notably, one realistic model display two distinct abrupt transitions in the same system. By tuning the range of the inter-module connectivity between these two limits, we further show that the order of the spatial transition changes gradually from continuous to abrupt. For the modular RR multiplex, we further characterize the spatial transition through its scaling behavior, revealing signatures of a mixed-order phase transition. In addition, we analytically determine the critical threshold at which modules become disconnected. Our results highlight the crucial role of modular organization and the critical role of interdependence in shaping network vulnerabilities under failures.
tldr: The paper analyzes two phase transitions in modular multiplex networks under percolation, comparing spatial and random-regular inter-module connectivity.
motivation: Modular critical infrastructures are often interdependent, and understanding how modular organization and multiplex interdependence affect failure cascades is important for network robustness.
method: The authors study percolation on modular multiplex networks with modules connected either as a 2D square lattice or a random regular network, using analytical and numerical characterization of transition thresholds and scaling behavior.
result: They find diverse transition behaviors, including two abrupt transitions in one realistic model, a gradual change from continuous to abrupt spatial transition when tuning inter-module connectivity range, and mixed-order scaling signatures for the modular random-regular multiplex case.
conclusion: The results highlight the crucial roles of modular organization and interdependence in shaping vulnerability and collapse in multiplex networks.

title: Higher-order Corrections To The Field Shift In Atomic Systems
authors: Z Harman And C H Keitel V A Yerokhin
abstract: Differences in nuclear charge distributions between isotopes lead to small changes in atomic spectra known as the field shift (FS). While largely proportional to the change in the mean-square nuclear radius, the FS also contains higher-order contributions with different dependencies on nuclear moments. Their knowledge is required in searches for new physics using King plots, since they contribute to deviations from King-plot linearity observed experimentally in recent studies. We present a systematic expansion of the field-shift energies in terms of nuclear parameters and test its validity against direct numerical calculations for H-like ions. We also compute leading- and higher-order field-shift corrections for alkali-like systems from Li-like to Rb-like ions, and find that their ratios are nearly independent of the ionic charge state, agreeing with the corresponding hydrogenic ratios on a sub-percent level. Motivated by these findings, we introduce an approximation in which these ratios are assumed to be independent of the electronic configuration. It is shown that, within this approximation, higher-order field-shift corrections do not induce King-plot nonlinearities. We conclude that only the small contributions beyond this approximation can contribute to the nonlinearities observed experimentally.
tldr: The paper systematically expands field-shift energies in atomic spectra to higher orders and shows that, under a configuration-independent ratio approximation, these corrections do not induce King-plot nonlinearities.
motivation: Higher-order field-shift contributions affect King-plot linearity used in searches for new physics, and their understanding is needed to interpret observed nonlinearities.
method: The authors derive a systematic expansion of field-shift energies in nuclear parameters and validate it against direct numerical calculations for H-like ions; they also compute corrections for alkali-like systems from Li-like to Rb-like ions.
result: Ratios of higher-order to leading field-shift corrections are nearly independent of ionic charge state and agree with hydrogenic ratios at sub-percent level; within the proposed approximation, higher-order corrections do not cause King-plot nonlinearities.
conclusion: Only small contributions beyond the configuration-independent ratio approximation can explain experimentally observed King-plot nonlinearities, constraining new-physics searches.

title: Spatiotemporal Mode-locked Fiber Lasers: Multidimensional Soliton Dynamics Revealed By Real-time Measurement
authors: Yi Zhou, Can Li, Zhuopeng Han, Kun Jin, Bo Ren, Zhenqiang Tang, Tao Wang, Zhiwen He, Jinyong Leng And Pu Zhou
abstract: Spatiotemporal mode-locked multimode fiber lasers have emerged as a promising platform for investigating nonlinear multidimensional physics, with prospective applications ranging from high-energy pulse generation and precise metrology to nonlinear microscopy. The fundamental mechanism governing ultrashort pulse formation in nonlinear multimode resonators, which can be interpreted as multidimensional dissipative solitons (MDSs), lies in spatiotemporal mode-locking (STML), which achieves synchronous locking of both temporal and spatial modes. In this review, the general principles of STML are initially elaborated, with a focus on MDS dynamics under real-time measurement. Subsequently, we summarize the operational principles of versatile real-time measurement techniques and recent advancements in characterizing the ultrafast transient MDS dynamics of STML lasers, including spatial mode switching, optical rogue waves, mode-locking buildup process, three-dimensional soliton molecules, soliton explosions, and breathing multimode solitons. Finally, we outline some perspectives on how real-time measurement methods could advance the study of multidimensional soliton dynamics in STML in the near future.
tldr: This review surveys spatiotemporal mode-locked multimode fiber lasers and real-time measurement of multidimensional dissipative soliton dynamics.
motivation: Spatiotemporal mode-locking in multimode fiber lasers offers a platform for nonlinear multidimensional physics and applications in pulse generation, metrology, and microscopy.
method: The authors review the general principles of spatiotemporal mode-locking and real-time measurement techniques used to characterize ultrafast transient soliton dynamics.
result: The review summarizes observed phenomena including spatial mode switching, optical rogue waves, mode-locking buildup, three-dimensional soliton molecules, soliton explosions, and breathing multimode solitons.
conclusion: The paper outlines future perspectives on using real-time measurement methods to advance the study of multidimensional soliton dynamics in spatiotemporal mode-locked lasers.

abstract: Higgs inflation, identifying the standard model (SM) Higgs boson as the, causes a unitarity issue during the preheating epoch after inflation in its simplest form, calling for a UV completion. Higgs– inflation serves as a natural candidate for the UV completion of Higgs inflation, providing a consistent framework to describe the inflationary dynamics till the end of reheating. Higgs– inflation contains a new scalar degree of freedom, the scalaron, which unitarizes the theory in the same way that the Higgs boson unitarizes the electroweak gauge boson scatterings in the SM. A particular emphasis is put on its particle physics aspects, such as the unitarity structure, frame-independence, and the renormalization group evolution.

motivation: Higgs inflation suffers from a unitarity problem during preheating in its simplest form, motivating a UV completion such as Higgs-R^2 inflation.
method: The review surveys the theoretical structure of Higgs-R^2 inflation, including the scalaron degree of freedom and its role in unitarizing inflationary dynamics through reheating.
result: Higgs-R^2 inflation provides a consistent framework for describing inflation until the end of reheating, with unitarity restored by the scalaron in analogy with electroweak unitarization.
conclusion: The paper is a particle-physics/cosmology review of Higgs-R^2 inflation and is not aligned with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems research directions.

title: Small-angle Solution Scattering: From Fundamental Theory To Practical Approximations
authors: Jan Skov Pedersen And Jochen S Hub Kristian Lytje
abstract: Small-angle scattering (SAS) with x-rays and neutrons is widely used in structural biology, soft matter, and colloidal science to probe molecular structures in solution. SAS rests on a single physical principle: wave interference from a distribution of scatterers. Yet the theoretical foundations of SAS are spread across the literature, often based on differing notation, definitions, and implicit assumptions. We present the theory of SAS in solution starting from the first Born approximation as a continuous derivation, spanning the scattering of a single electron to the observed intensity of a molecular solution and its comparison with atomistic structural models. The derivation is explicit throughout—approximations, averaging procedures, and algebraic manipulations are stated rather than assumed—and the resulting expressions are independent of the probe (x-ray or neutron) and apply to both rigid and flexible molecules. The framework resolves several ambiguities in the current literature, notably the role of background subtraction as a theoretical rather than a purely experimental operation and the role of boundary cross-terms in justifying that subtraction. A central result is that analytical scattering calculations and approaches based on explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, typically treated as distinct traditions, are realizations of the common theoretical framework derived here. As the precision and reproducibility of SAS data continue to increase, this comprehensive framework provides a basis for integrating theory, simulation, and experiment in future developments of SAS.
tldr: A comprehensive, self-contained derivation of small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering theory in solution, from the first Born approximation to comparison with atomistic structural models.
motivation: The theoretical foundations of small-angle scattering are scattered across literature with inconsistent notation and implicit assumptions, creating ambiguities about background subtraction and the relationship between analytical and simulation-based approaches.
method: The authors build a continuous, explicit derivation starting from the first Born approximation, tracking approximations and averaging procedures from single-electron scattering to the observed intensity of a molecular solution, keeping the treatment probe-independent and valid for rigid and flexible molecules.
result: The framework resolves literature ambiguities—notably showing background subtraction is a theoretical rather than purely experimental operation justified by boundary cross-terms—and demonstrates that analytical scattering calculations and explicit-solvent molecular dynamics are realizations of one common theory.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a basis for integrating theory, simulation, and experiment in small-angle scattering as data precision and reproducibility increase.

tldr: This study uses insurance claims data from 245 million US patients to revise estimates of the types and duration of Long COVID symptoms, correcting for misattribution biases in commonly used study designs.
motivation: Many existing Long COVID studies misattribute symptoms to COVID-19 when they are actually caused by non-COVID conditions that prompted care-seeking and testing, leading to inflated or distorted estimates of symptom prevalence and persistence.
method: The authors analyze large-scale medical claims records covering 245 million US patients, applying statistical/epidemiological designs (likely including negative-control or matched-cohort comparisons) to separate genuine post-COVID sequelae from background care-seeking effects.
result: The analysis yields revised estimates of the types and duration of Long COVID symptoms that differ from earlier claims-based figures, indicating that some prior estimates overstate the burden attributable to COVID-19.
conclusion: Careful study design is essential when using claims data to quantify Long COVID; the revised estimates provide a more accurate picture of symptom types and persistence at national scale.
